items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: there was a fellow by the name of Danny Moss, a fine tenor player I played with the other night

ctx.x: Copenhagen or whatever, and he came over and we had this agent, got together a thing called -- now, Eddie Miller was in Europe, playing with Alex Welch, and I had just finished the 28 straight days with the Jazz of the Swing Era and they went back to the states and Eddie Lockjaw Davis, Ben Webster, Eddie Miller and I went on this thing called Just for Tenor, you know, it was a concert, we did about eight concerts, and then they went back to the States and I went into Ronnie Scott's for the first -- well, I think…

At the end, there was a fellow by the name of Danny Moss, a fine tenor player I played with the other night, and Ronnie Scott, who is a fine player, and at the end -- I did three shows there a night -- and at the end of each show we'd use the three tenors for a finale which was a marvelous thing. People loved it.
Then back to the States and it's difficult to remember what I did, except that I went back to work to do concerts for George.
